title: What is the smallest multiple of all these numbers?
description: The board writes each number from the list as a multiplication of primes, takes the most times each prime appears in any one number, and multiplies them to get the lowest common multiple. It then checks that every number in the list divides the result.
teaching_notes: One idea: the lowest common multiple of many numbers takes each prime the most times it appears in any one of them. Watch for children who multiply all the numbers together.

source: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10?
video_script.why: The child can find a lowest common multiple of two numbers from their primes and now does it for nine numbers.
video_script.substitution: The smallest multiple of all the numbers takes each prime the most times it appears in any one of them.
video_script.anchor: a row of nine number cards, one, two, three, four, five, six, eight, nine and ten
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest such number is three hundred and sixty

final_answer.spoken: the smallest such number is three hundred and sixty

maths_rules: most 2s: three, in 8; most 3s: two, in 9; most 5s: one, in 5 and 10
LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 8 x 9 x 5
check: 8, 9 and 5 are factors of 8 x 9 x 5; 10 = 2 x 5 and 6 = 2 x 3 fit inside; 4 and 2 are inside 8, 3 is inside 9, 1 divides everything
video_script.design: Nine numbers in a row, each written as a multiplication of primes, then the most of each prime. Assumes the lowest common multiple of two numbers from their primes. The reference to the earlier grade in the book's question is left out.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a row of nine number cards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and an empty answer box

marks.m1: the small title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the nine number cards appear in a row
marks.m3: a question mark glows in the answer box

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about one number and many divisors.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The numbers are one, two, three, four, five, six, eight, nine and ten.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>What is the smallest number that all of them divide exactly?

beats.on_screen: the number cards stay on the board and Keeko sits beside them

marks.m1: Keeko sits beside the number cards

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a block of primes for one number is drawn; a bigger block holds the blocks of several numbers; the smallest bigger block keeps the most of each prime

marks.m1: a block of primes for one number is drawn
marks.m2: a bigger block holds the prime blocks of several numbers
marks.m3: the smallest bigger block keeps the most copies of each prime

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A multiple of a number contains all the primes of that number.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>To be a multiple of many numbers, it must contain the primes of each one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smallest such number takes the most times each prime appears in any one of them.

marks.m1: the nine numbers are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the numbers are one, two, three, four, five, six, eight, nine and ten.

beats.on_screen: To find: the smallest number that is a multiple of all of them

marks.m1: the words the smallest multiple of all of them are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the smallest number that is a multiple of all of them.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: prime factors. 2 = 2; 3 = 3; 4 = 2 x 2; 5 = 5; 6 = 2 x 3; 8 = 2 x 2 x 2; 9 = 3 x 3; 10 = 2 x 5. The number 1 has no prime.

marks.m1: the heading prime factors is written
marks.m5: 2 = 2, 3 = 3 and 5 = 5 are written and 1 is marked no prime

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, write each number as a multiplication of primes.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four is two times two, and six is two times three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eight is two times two times two.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Nine is three times three, and ten is two times five.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Two, three and five are primes already, and one has no prime.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the most of each prime. 2: three times, in 8. 3: two times, in 9. 5: one time, in 5 and 10.

marks.m1: the heading most of each prime is written
marks.m2: 2: three times, in 8 is written and the three 2s in 8 are circled
marks.m3: 3: two times, in 9 is written and the two 3s in 9 are circled
marks.m4: 5: one time, in 5 and 10 is written and the 5 is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take the most times each prime appears in one number.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The prime two appears most in eight, three times.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The prime three appears most in nine, two times.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The prime five appears most in five and in ten, once.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: LCM = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 8 x 9 x 5

marks.m1: 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 is written from the circled primes
marks.m2: the twos are grouped into 8, the threes into 9, and 8 x 9 x 5 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, multiply these primes together. That is two times two times two, times three times three, times five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Group the twos and the threes, and we get eight times nine times five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check. 8, 9 and 5 are factors of 8 x 9 x 5. 10 = 2 x 5 and 6 = 2 x 3 fit inside. 4 and 2 are inside 8, 3 is inside 9, 1 divides everything.

marks.m2: 8, 9 and 5 are ticked in 8 x 9 x 5
marks.m3: 10 = 2 x 5 and 6 = 2 x 3 are shown fitting inside and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Check that every number in the list divides it.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight, nine and five are factors of eight times nine times five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten is two times five, and six is two times three, and both fit inside.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Four and two are inside eight, three is inside nine, and one divides everything.

marks.m1: 8 x 9 x 5 turns into 360 and is boxed
marks.m2: 8 x 9 = 72 and 72 x 5 = 360 are written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The smallest such number is three hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight times nine is seventy two, and seventy two times five is three hundred and sixty.
